title: Knowledge in the book
hook: the first word is read, and knowledge is praised throughout

segments.voice: Yesterday, shifa', and your line: a healing. Did you tuck one verse away for a low moment? Today, a theme that starts with the very first word revealed. Day six hundred sixty-eight.

If you had to guess the first word of a holy book's revelation, you might guess pray, or believe, or obey. In the Islamic account, the angel Jibril comes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in a cave on Mount Hira, and the first word is none of those. It's iqra'. Read. Or recite. Surah ninety-six, in Pickthall's translation: "Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth." A revelation whose first word is read. And from there, knowledge runs through the whole of it.

The word is 'ilm, knowledge. Its root, '-l-m, gives a whole family. 'Alim, one who knows; its plural, 'ulama', the scholars. Mu'allim, a teacher. And al-'Alim, the All-Knowing, one of the names of Allah. Trace the theme through the book. In al-Baqarah, the first human, Adam, is honored by being taught: Allah taught him the names of all things, and the angels admit they know only what they've been taught. In surah thirty-nine comes a question that doesn't need answering: "Are those who know equal with those who know not?" In surah fifty-eight, Allah raises in degrees those who believe and those given knowledge. And in surah twenty, the Prophet himself is told to ask for one thing, more of it. "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge." Some commentators note it's the only thing he is told to ask more of. The hadith carry it on. One, in Ibn Majah, says seeking knowledge is a duty on every Muslim. Another, in Sahih Muslim, says whoever walks a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for them a path to the Garden. And here's a thing people repeat that isn't in the sources: seek knowledge even as far as China. It's often quoted, and hadith scholars judged it weak or invented. Which is itself a lesson in 'ilm. Knowing includes checking. Muslim scholars built a whole science around asking who said a thing, and whether it was really said.

The practice: learn something today. Use this sit to plant it. Breathe, and ask yourself: what's one thing I'd like to understand better? A word from this year's lessons, a skill, a question about someone you love. Pick it and hold it. If you pray, you can say the Prophet's line from surah twenty: my Lord, increase me in knowledge. Then decide when, before tonight, you'll spend ten minutes on it. The bell holds the time.
'Ilm. Knowledge, from '-l-m, the root of scholar, teacher and the All-Knowing: what the Prophet is told to ask more of. Today's word.
Your line: seek knowledge. Today, before you pass on one thing you heard, a fact, a quote, a hadith, check where it came from. Day six hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Muslims treat seeking knowledge as a religious duty; some recite "my Lord, increase me in knowledge" (20:114) before study, and hadith scholarship developed careful methods for checking who transmitted a report.

fork.setup: in surah twenty, the Prophet is told to ask his Lord to increase him in one thing. what is it?
fork.reveal: knowledge: my Lord, increase me in knowledge. some commentators note it's the only thing he's told to ask more of.

original.note: Arabic: knowledge. the same root gives 'alim, 'ulama' and al-'Alim.

trapdoor: what you thought: religion is about faith, not knowledge.
what it means: the Qur'an opens with read, honors Adam by teaching him, and has the Prophet ask for more knowledge.
what a scholar hears: the famous China saying is judged weak; hadith science (isnad criticism) exists because knowing includes checking.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): 'a book whose first word is read' corrected to 'a revelation' (iqra' is the first word revealed, not the book's first word); 'the only thing he's told to ask more of' now attributed to commentators in teach and fork; the Prophet named with the honorific; 'many recite' softened.
Pickthall wording of 96:1, 39:9 and 20:114 quoted from memory; please confirm each.
'The only thing in the Qur'an he's told to ask to have increased' is a common observation (e.g. Ibn Kathir's remark on 20:114); confirm.
Hadith numbers cited from memory (Ibn Majah 224; Muslim 2699); the 'China' saying's grading (weak or fabricated) should be confirmed.
First revelation at Hira as in the hadith of Aisha (Sahih al-Bukhari 3); not separately cited in sources.
